history.summary: A 1,538 sqft '4BR' (really 4 bed / 3 bath) at The Clearwater, 8 Bedok Reservoir View, asking $2.05M / $1,333 psf after a $2.15M -> $2.05M cut in 65 unsold days. The project is genuinely sound - DT30 Bedok Reservoir on the doorstep, 420 units, 436 resales with 87.1% profitable, REALSCORE 3.7 - but the price carries no margin of safety. Benchmarked against same-size prints rather than the project or district median, the ask is only 2-3% under fair value, and this exact 1,538 sqft layout has not printed ONCE in 70 URA transactions over five years. The headline '-12% vs district median' is D16's Bayshore-vs-reservoir split, not value.
history.rating_rationale: Neutral because the single strongest backtested forward lever - cheap versus peers - is neutral here once the size-mix artifact is removed, and the offsetting risk is an untested exit. Size-adjusting the seven closest recent comps to 1,538 sqft (elasticity -0.19; in-project measured -0.138) gives fair value of ~$1,364 psf / $2.10M, so the $1,333 psf ask is only -2.3% cheap - inside noise. The -12.0% psf_premium_vs_ura_median is measured against D16's $1,532 median, which is set by Bayshore / Costa Del Sol / Bedok Residences / new-launch stock at $2,000-$3,300 psf; inland Bedok Reservoir is a permanently cheaper sub-market (Aquarius $1,342, Clearwater $1,401 vs Waterfront Key $1,722), so that gap is a location level, not a dislocation. The nearest true comp is Aquarius by the Park, Aug-25, 1,539 sqft - one sqft off - at $1,306 psf; the subject asks +2% over it. Against that thin value case sits real exit risk: zero prints at 1,538 sqft in five years, a project where psf falls hard with size (2,443 sqft printed $1,187 and 2,486 sqft $1,098 against $1,400-$1,516 for 1,227-1,367 sqft), and revealed buyer preference - a 1,389 sqft unit sold for exactly $2.05M in Jul-26 at a record $1,476 psf while this larger unit sat unsold and cut its price. Buyers here took less space for the same money. Lease is 70 years remaining (not the 72 the record carries; 99 yrs from 18/07/1997), so a 5-7yr hold exits at 63-65 years with the next buyer facing the 60-year financing edge. Not an Avoid: nothing is broken, transit is excellent, the exit record is good, and trailing appreciation is real rather than mix-driven (the 1,378 sqft stack alone went $1,089 -> $1,354 psf, ~5.9%/yr). At roughly $1.90-1.95M ($1,235-$1,270 psf) - below the Aquarius same-size comp - this becomes genuinely interesting. At $2.05M the buyer is paying fair value for the project's least-traded layout and taking the illiquidity for free.
red_flags: The exact 1,538 sqft layout has ZERO prints in the project's 70 URA transactions 2021-2026. Traded sizes are 657/678/710/947/980/1001/1195/1227/1259/1313/1335/1356/1367/1378/1389/1410/1442/1453/1905/1916/2422/2443/2486 - the subject's size is absent. Exit is into an untested segment.

No real value margin. Size-adjusted to 1,538 sqft, the seven closest recent comps median $1,364 psf vs the $1,333 ask = -2.3% (-3.0% using the in-project measured elasticity). The strongest backtested forward lever is effectively neutral.

The -12.0% psf_premium_vs_ura_median is a sub-market artifact, not value: D16's $1,532 median is set by Bayshore/East Coast stock printing $2,000-$3,300 psf (Vela Bay $3,302, Pinery $2,575, Costa Del Sol $2,108). Inland Bedok Reservoir structurally trades $1,300-$1,450. Same pattern as the D23 Hillview/CCK split.

MMR's psf_value 5.24 and age_value 5.06 credit is size-mix driven - psf_cohort_txns is only 4. This unit is near the top of the project's size range, and psf falls steeply with size here: 2,443 sqft printed $1,187 and 2,486 sqft $1,098 against $1,400-$1,516 for 1,227-1,367 sqft.

Revealed market preference against the layout: a 1,389 sqft unit sold for exactly $2,050,000 on 14 Jul 2026 at a record $1,476 psf, while this 1,538 sqft unit at the same $2.05M has sat unsold. Buyers chose 149 fewer sqft for identical money.

Seller cut $2,150,000 -> $2,050,000 (-4.7%) over 65 days (8 Jun -> 12 Aug 2026) without a sale, during a window in which the project set new psf highs. Either motivated seller or an unseen unit-specific defect.

Lease is 70 years remaining, not the 72 in the record (99 yrs from 18/07/1997, per realsmart and the URA tenure string). A 5-7yr hold exits at 63-65 years, and the buyer after that faces the 60-year CPF/financing edge. MMR's lease component is already -3.2.

Competing standing inventory inside the project in the same money band: a 1,335 sqft 3BR at $2.00M, a 1,388 sqft 3BR at $2.10M, a 1,436 sqft 3BR at $2.278M, plus a SECOND 1,538 sqft 4BR asking $2.25M - against only ~10-15 resales a year project-wide. (The four identical $1,999,999 listings are one unit multi-listed by four agents, shared unit_group 'the clearwater|3|363' - not four units.)

Floor, facing and stack are entirely unverified: floor_level is null, facing is unobtainable from PropertyGuru, and no profile exists for The Clearwater. Reservoir-view vs internal/west-facing is a large value swing in this project and cannot be checked from this data - a 65-day-unsold ask invites the question.
Yield is thin: 3.31% gross / 1.77% net on $5,660/mo (36 URA contracts); realsmart independently puts the project at ~3.2% ($3.86 rent psf, median rent $4,800). Weak carry for a 5-7yr hold.

13% of the project's resale history lost money - 57 unprofitable against 379 profitable of 436. The realsmart page's '100% Profitable' badge is the marketing highlights tile, NOT the real count; the true figure is 87.1%.
The building is 24-25 years old (TOP 2001) and MMR already books a very_old_property flag - capex/MCST risk over the hold, with no en-bloc catalyst identified.

Trailing appreciation of 5.72%/yr (70 txns) is real but carries ~zero forward power per the repo's own backtest - it is story, not signal, and should not be extrapolated into the ROI projection's 5.4-5.5%/yr.
catalysts: Genuinely excellent transit: DT30 Bedok Reservoir is 350m / 4 min per the listing and 60m per realsmart's measure - among the closest MRT distances in the OCR book, and MRT proximity is one of the few levers with measured (if modest) forward power (std_beta -0.11 as-of-T).
OCR - the region with the strongest realized forward returns in the full 28-district panel (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%).

Strong exit record on a trustworthy sample: 87.1% of 436 resales sold at a profit (379 vs 57), avg holding 9 years, REALSCORE 3.7/5, avg annualized profit 5.1%. Well above the 150-resale trust bar - good downside evidence that this project has not lost owners money.
Deep, liquid project: 420 units, 849 total transactions since 1999, ~10-19 resales/yr, $672.1M transacted - buyer-pool depth survives clustering in the backtest (std_beta +0.16).

Deep HDB-upgrader catchment (62% HDB buyers) with three primary schools inside 1km - Yu Neng 362m, Red Swastika 381m, St Anthony's Canossian 745m - supporting the family bid that is the natural exit for a 4-bedroom.

Trailing appreciation is genuine rather than a size-mix artifact: the 1,378 sqft stack alone went $1,089 psf (Dec-21) -> $1,354 psf (Sep-25), ~5.9%/yr, and project median psf ran $1,068 (2021) -> $1,418 (2026). Treat as evidence the project participates in the cycle, not as a forward forecast.
Most space per dollar in the current inland-D16 large-unit set: $2.05M buys 1,538 sqft here vs 1,432-1,464 sqft at The Bayshore/East Meadows/Urban Vista for $1.99-2.05M.

D16 new-launch supply is tight and priced far above: Bedok Rise Residences (awarded Dec-2025 at $1,330 psf ppr, ~380 units, launching 2H-2027, TOP 2031-32) will price near $2,400+ psf, widening the resale gap. Per the repo's backtest the future-infrastructure/new-supply story has no measured forward power - narrative, not edge.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Thin but honest. $5,660/mo estimated from 36 URA project contracts (confidence 0.8, not capped) = 3.31% gross / 1.77% net. realsmart independently gives $3.86 rent psf and a $4,800 median rent across 12-17 quoted contracts, implying ~$5,940 for 1,538 sqft and ~3.2-3.5% gross - the two sources agree. No yield artifact here: this is a normal, unexciting large-unit OCR yield, and at 1.77% net the carry does not meaningfully fund the hold. Count it as carry, never as appreciation - the panel shows high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16).
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 5.72%/yr ura_5yr_cagr (70 txns, confidence 1.0) is unusually well-supported for once - I checked it is not the pooled size-mix artifact this repo has been burned by: the single 1,378 sqft stack independently ran $1,089 -> $1,354 psf (Dec-21 to Sep-25, ~5.9%/yr), matching the pooled median's $1,068 -> $1,418 (2021-2026). So the trailing number is real. That still does not make it a forecast - trailing CAGR has ~zero marginal forward power once clustered. For a 5-7yr hold I override to 4.0%/yr: the OCR realized forward baseline is +3.7%, this project earns a small premium for doorstep DT30 and a deep buyer pool, offset by 70-year lease decay on a 24-year-old asset and the steep large-unit psf penalty inside the project. The ROI table's 5.4-5.5%/yr annualized is therefore optimistic by roughly 150bp; at 4.0% the 5yr exit is ~$2.49M rather than $2.67M, closer to the sensitivity table's downside case.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile exists for The Clearwater (status: not_researched) and floor_level/facing are null, so the unit's floor, orientation and reservoir-view status are unverified - a material gap in a project whose value swings on whether a stack faces the reservoir or the internal carpark/west. What can be said from URA: the 1,538 sqft size does not appear in any of the project's 70 prints 2021-2026, so this is a rare stack with no direct trading history. The DB records 4 baths; 99.co and PropertyGuru both show 4 bed / 3 bath, so treat the bath count as 3. The layout is confirmed real and repeated - a second 1,538 sqft 4BR is asking $2.25M ($1,463 psf) - so this is not a mis-scrape, just an illiquid format. bed_bands returns 'unknown' (no 4BR band for this project), which is honest rather than a pass: note that one published unit mix puts the project's 4BR floor plans at 2,303-2,433 sqft and 3BR at 1,195-1,905 sqft, which would make this a large 3BR-format unit marketed as a 4-bedder. Unresolved, and it matters for the family-buyer exit bid - worth confirming against the floor plan before any offer.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: OCR realized forward baseline (+3.7%/yr, full 28-district panel) plus a small premium for doorstep DT30 and deep buyer pool, less 70-yr lease decay and the project's steep large-unit psf penalty. Trailing 5.72% verified as real (not a size-mix artifact) but per repo priors carries ~zero forward power, so it is not extrapolated.

history.summary: 3BR 1,335 sqft mid-floor unit at The Clearwater (D16, 420 units, 99yr from 1997, TOP 2001), 284m from Bedok Reservoir DTL, asking $1.888M / $1,414 psf. That is exactly the market: the five most recent same-size (1,335–1,367 sqft) prints from Jun-2025 to Jan-2026 cleared at $1.87–1.95M ($1,386–1,426 psf), mostly on floors 6–10. The age-adjusted district benchmark puts it at −1.7%, so it isn't cheap. The exit record is strong, the resale market is deep, and rent covers a 3.1% gross carry. The lease is the drag: about 70 years left today and about 63–65 at a 5–7yr exit.
history.rating_rationale: The price is fair but has no value edge. $1,414 psf matches the project's own recent prints for this size ($1.87–1.88M for 1,335 sqft in Jun–Nov 2025), and relative_value is −1.7% vs age-adjusted D16 peers. Cheap-vs-district-peers is the robust forward signal, and it is missing here. What drives the 701 score is mostly trailing appreciation (5.8% CAGR, de-weighted), the MRT, and transaction depth. Transaction depth is real, and the downside is well evidenced: REALSCORE 3.7, 87.1% of 436 resale pairs profitable, 5.1%/yr average. Against that, the lease falls to ~63–65yr by exit, which thins the next buyer's CPF/financing pool, and prices have already re-rated about 30% since late 2021. At least four other listings show the same 3BR/1,335 sqft at $1.89M after repeated price cuts. That points to seller overhang, so a buyer has room to negotiate towards ~$1.80–1.83M, which also brings it inside the his-mandate budget. It would still only be a fair-price unit at that level, not a Buy.
red_flags: No discount: $1,414 psf is in line with the project's own last-12-month same-size prints ($1,386–1,426 psf); −1.7% vs age-adjusted D16 median
99yr lease from 1997: ~70yr left now, ~63–65yr at a 5–7yr exit, so the next buyer's financing/CPF pool narrows and lease decay accelerates
Price already up ~30% since Dec-2021 (1,335 sqft: $1.44M then, $1.88M in 2025); trailing momentum is story, not a forward signal
Several identical 3BR/1,335 sqft listings at $1.89M with 3–6 price cuts each: supply overhang, soft asking market
$1.888M is ~5% over the his-mandate $1.8M ceiling unless negotiated down
Aged 2001 build: maintenance/upgrading cost exposure
catalysts: 284m to Bedok Reservoir DTL station, opposite Bedok Reservoir Park
Deep, liquid resale market: 69 URA prints in ~5yr, 420 units, mostly 3BR stock (304 units), so the exit is proven
Downside record: 87.1% of 436 resale pairs profitable (REALSCORE 3.7, 5.1%/yr average)
OCR region, the strongest measured forward region

Seller overhang gives negotiating leverage below $1.85M
